note: Added 2026-09-09 together with 13 sibling Greater Vancouver property tax notices, on request, to grow `propertytax` coverage from 6 documents to 20. The SECOND City of North Vancouver notice (458 9TH ST E), a different roll from property_north_van_city. total_invoice_amount is the COLUMN A (no home owner grant) figure -- the amount payable when no grant is claimed, which is the column the pipeline chose on all 14 new notices. A=7,192.89 / B=6,622.89 / C=6,347.89. Arrears and delinquent both print 0.00, so nothing is carried forward and the Total Amount Due IS this bill's own charges -- the control for the carried-forward case on its sibling. || invoice_date is NOT asserted: this notice prints no issue-date label, so build_write_values substitutes date.today() and the scaffold captured the run date (2026-09-09) -- a false green that would flip red tomorrow. Same reason as property_surrey. || invoice_description NOT asserted: free-text that rewords itself every run. || The narrative fields (diagnosis_solution, recommendation, warranty and their zh_hant twins) are blank by policy on a municipal bill. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice.
